hdmi_rx.description: An HDMI/DVI receiver: a TMDS link in, parallel video out -- pixel clock, lock, data enable, syncs, 24 data bits. Every implementation offers these same ports, so the bayerlink receiver and the designs above it do not change when it does. How it is configured on a board, and which pins it lands on, is that board's.

link_khz.description: The link's pixel clock, in kHz: the rate the source sends, which the implementation's clocking is set for.

status.description: 1: the implementation's own account of the link, on the ports below marked by it -- for an implementation that keeps one.

inputs.name: TMDS
inputs.description: The link, from the jack's pins.

inputs.name: refclk
inputs.description: The reference clock the implementation calibrates its input delays with; its frequency is the implementation's fact refclk_mhz.

outputs.name: pclk
outputs.description: The clock recovered from the link: it stops when the cable is pulled.

outputs.name: bonded
outputs.description: tmds_rx: the three lanes found in step.

outputs.name: clock_locked
outputs.description: tmds_rx: its clock manager locked to the link's clock.

outputs.name: aligned
outputs.description: tmds_rx: each lane aligned, lane 0 lowest.

outputs.name: eye
outputs.description: tmds_rx: each lane's eye, its taps that misread nothing, 5 bits a lane, lane 0 lowest.

outputs.name: slip
outputs.description: tmds_rx: each lane's bit slip, 4 bits a lane, lane 0 lowest.

outputs.name: survey_count
outputs.description: tmds_rx's survey, an entry at a time, each entry's fields together (hdl/tmds_rx.v): the misread tokens at this lane, slip and tap, 255 for no blank seen.

outputs.name: survey_lane_tap
outputs.description: The tap that lane samples at.

outputs.name: survey_lane_slip
outputs.description: The bit slip that lane samples at.

dvi2rgb.description: Digilent's dvi2rgb on a 7-series part: TMDS decoded in the fabric (ISERDESE2, IDELAYE2, an MMCM). Needs Digilent's vivado-library in the IP catalogue. Lane map solved 2026-08-12 on a PYNQ-Z2 with the picam2hdmi source, counting and checker patterns: it follows this IP's bus order, not the board, so it holds on any board receiving through dvi2rgb. kClkRange follows the link: its MMCM multiplies the link clock by 5 x kClkRange and divides by kClkRange, so the five-times serial clock is the same whatever the range, and the range only keeps the VCO inside its 600-1200 MHz specification -- range 1 at a 74.25 MHz link would run it at 371 MHz. Range 2 at 74.25 MHz judged 30/30 frames bit-exact on the PYNQ-Z2 (2026-10-09). Below 25 MHz it has no range.

config.kClkRange: 1 if link_khz >= 120000 else 2 if link_khz >= 60000 else 3 if link_khz >= 40000 else 4 if link_khz >= 30000 else 5

tmds_rx.description: bayerlink-fpga's own TMDS receiver on a 7-series part (hdl/tmds_rx.v): an MMCM at five times the link clock into BUFIO and BUFR, an IDELAYE2 and a pair of ISERDESE2 a lane, and an alignment made for links that blank every line -- each delay tap of every bit slip given tens of lines to show blanks and count misread tokens, not 50 ms, so a mode change costs a fraction of a second rather than seconds, and each lane samples between the walls of its eye at the least delay -- then the lanes bonded by where their blanking ends, and decoded. Its lanes are the TMDS channels in order. RANGE keeps the MMCM's VCO in specification, as dvi2rgb's kClkRange does.

config.RANGE: 1 if link_khz >= 120000 else 2 if link_khz >= 60000 else 3 if link_khz >= 40000 else 4 if link_khz >= 30000 else 5
